newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds pick up then settle down for budget.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds pick up then settle down for budget.

text.p: Irish bonds picked up on a ripple of early buying interest on Wednesday and then settled down, with all eyes focused on the 1997 budget, due to be delivered by finance minister Ruairi Quinn from 1545 GMT.
The 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was yielding 5.74 percent by 1445 GMT on Wednesday, down from 5.81 late on Tuesday.
The benchmark 8.0 percent stock due 2006 also picked up, its yield narrowing to 6.50 from 6.55 percent before Tuesday's close.
"The market's had a reasonable day but volumes are light with the budget in view," one dealer said.
"We saw some early buyers of five- and 10-year paper, the five-year in particular has perform well of late. But we've pretty much tracked the move in Bunds," she added.
The 10-year spread of Irish bonds over German Bunds was hardly changed at 82 basis points. The March Bund future trading in London was 30 basis points higher at 101.75 by 1445 GMT.

The Irish market was also supported by UK gilts, which were buoyed by a sharp fall in December UK retail sales. The March gilt future was 24/32 higher at 111-20, having shot up after official data showed December sales off 0.8 percent, confirming anecdotal evidence of a disappointing Christmas for retailers.

But for the Irish market, it was all eyes down for the budget, although an expansionary package offering tax cuts of up to 400 million punts in value was widely discounted. "It is really all about the EBR but people have priced in an expansionary budget so it won't have too much effect on the bond market," one trader said.
Economists forecast Quinn will announce a 1997 Exchange Borrowing Requirement between 600 and 750 million Irish pounds.
"It's all been well signalled in advance," the trader said.
